gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the '60W × 2' on the Yamaha A-S301 card and the '60W × 2' on the WiiM Amp Pro card are different kinds of rating. Yamaha's figure is full-band continuous power (20 Hz–20 kHz, 0.019% THD, 8 Ω). WiiM's product page and FAQ give 60 W/8 Ω and 120 W/4 Ω with no THD or bandwidth condition at all. At 4 Ω, none of the four picks is rated on the same basis.
standout_why: I compared against recordplayeradvice.com (Denon vs Yamaha), which gives 45 W and 60 W with no test conditions and says only that Denon's 70 W is a 4-ohm figure 'not directly comparable'. hifiaudiosource.com (Yamaha vs Denon) already lines up Yamaha's 20–20k / 0.019% against Denon's 20–20k / 0.07% and warns that the two 4-ohm figures are measured differently, so that half is already taken. Neither page mentions the WiiM Amp Pro or the Marantz Model 50. I found no result that says WiiM's 60/120 W has no stated condition or puts all four picks in one table. I could not open the whathifi.com, stylusandsound.com or B&H compare pages within the call budget, so they are unchecked.
decides: The pick stays the same, but the reason a shopper might choose between ChatGPT's two '60W' cards goes away. The only figures on a shared basis are Yamaha 60 W against Denon 45 W, both full-band at 8 Ω. That gap is 10·log10(60/45) ≈ 1.25 dB, so power should not decide between them. The WiiM's 60 W cannot be ranked against either one from the maker's specs. Shoppers with 4-ohm or low-sensitivity speakers should not read Denon 70 W, Yamaha 140 W, WiiM 120 W or Marantz 100 W as a ladder, because each is a different measurement.

findings.note: Quoted: 'Output power 4 Ohm (1 kHz, T.H.D. 0.7%) 70 W'. This is a single-frequency test at 10× the distortion allowed in the 8 Ω rating, so it is not a doubling of the 45 W figure.
